story.eyebrow: From hidden cost to clear decisions
story.title: See the workshop through real numbers, not assumptions.
story.body: ElecIO brings program transfer, file storage, and performance reporting into one orderly flow—giving production a smoother path and management evidence it can actually review.

steps.label: STEP 01 — SEE THE REAL PICTURE
steps.title: Runtime and downtime stop being a blind spot.
steps.body: Every program run is timestamped. That means you can see which machine was productive and where time was lost without relying on verbal updates or assigning another person to track it.

steps.label: STEP 02 — SIMPLIFY THE INFRASTRUCTURE
steps.title: Management becomes central; the machine side becomes lighter.
steps.body: Instead of a PC, serial card, and long cable at every control, one ElecIO unit sits beside each machine while files are distributed from a central station over the workshop network.
points: Central access from one PC or phone
A short, fixed serial cable at the control
Fewer failure points and fewer trips across the floor

steps.label: STEP 03 — PROTECT THE PRODUCTION FLOW
steps.title: A network interruption should not stop machining.
steps.body: Every unit has its own internal storage. The program remains at the machine, so a temporary network issue does not make the control completely dependent on a central connection.
points: Keep working with the locally stored file
Return to central management when connectivity resumes

outcomes.title: Guess less. Invest with better evidence.
outcomes.body: ElecIO is more than wireless transfer. It gives management a more orderly view of infrastructure, production activity, and the areas worth improving next.

story.title: The technical details should be clear before installation.
story.body: An ElecIO deployment starts with accurate controller identification, continues with the right communication profile, and ends with a traceable transfer path and independent storage beside the machine.

steps.label: STEP 01 — IDENTIFY THE CONTROL
steps.title: Match the model, port, and transfer method before deployment.
steps.body: Final compatibility is more specific than a controller brand. The control model, port condition, and existing parameters are reviewed so the right connection method is established for that machine.
points: Evaluate FANUC, SIEMENS, HEIDENHAIN, and other controls
Match port type and machine condition
No blanket compatibility claim without verification

steps.label: STEP 02 — CONFIGURE THE PROTOCOL
steps.title: Serial parameters follow the logic of your control.
steps.body: Software and hardware flow control, serial transfer, and the LSV2 route are selected around the control—so deployment follows technical requirements instead of unlimited trial and error.
points: LSV2 and TNC Server for compatible use cases

steps.label: STEP 03 — TRANSFER AND OBSERVE
steps.title: The right file reaches the right machine with visible status.
steps.body: ElecIO Manager organizes programs and exposes transfer state. Each unit also has independent internal storage, keeping the program close to the control that consumes it.

outcomes.title: More predictable deployment. More precise support.
outcomes.body: Clear communication details and an independent unit at each machine help the new system enter production without creating another central point of failure.

items.title: A defined communication profile

items.body: An isolated circuit between the control and communication equipment reduces risk from electrical potential differences and noise.
